name: Jira
one_liner: Atlassian Jira Cloud issue tracking and project management product with a REST API.
auth_notes: OAuth 2.0 (3LO) authorization code apps created in developer console; basic auth with account email plus API token for scripts (passwords deprecated). Atlassian discourages collecting API tokens in distributed apps.
access_notes: Jira has a Free pricing tier; API tokens and 3LO apps are self-serve. Plan-level API gating not found. Rate limits are points-based per hour, enforced from 2 Mar 2026.

buildability.rationale: Documented REST v3 with self-serve OAuth 3LO and API tokens; official Atlassian MCP exists. Caveats: per-site consent, points-based rate limits, Atlassian discourages per-customer token apps.

auth.quote: This page shows you how REST clients can authenticate themselves using basic authentication with an Atlassian account email address and API token.
OAuth 2.0 (3LO) allows external applications and services to access Atlassian product APIs on a user's behalf.

access.quote: Jira pricing: Free, Standard, Premium, Enterprise | Atlassian

api_surface.quote: You can use Jira webhooks to notify your app or web application when certain events occur in Jira.
When any limit is exceeded, Jira returns an HTTP 429 Too Many Requests response.
The Jira REST API enables you to interact with Jira programmatically.

mcp.quote: The official Atlassian MCP Server is a cloud-based bridge between your Atlassian Cloud site and compatible external tools.

buildability.quote: Apps that collect API tokens or instruct customers to create individual 3LO apps don't comply with our Security requirements for cloud apps

identity.quote: This documentation is for version 3 of the Jira Cloud platform REST API, which is the latest version.

disputes.why: Atlassian's own GitHub org publishes the official MCP server at mcp.atlassian.com.
First pass used a third-party repo.
Self-serve API tokens/3LO and Free tier; documented rate limits.
Free tier plus self-serve API tokens; medium confidence.
